html:
The first written recipes for gunpowder, set down in the Wujing Zongyao, a military manual compiled for the Song court in 1044. Gunpowder is a mix of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal, the first known chemical explosive.

Daoist alchemists in China came across the mixture while looking for medicines, probably in the 9th century. By the early 10th century it was used in war. The 1044 manual gave several formulas and described weapons built on them: fire arrows, incendiary bombs thrown by catapult and smoke weapons. Its mixes burned fast rather than exploding hard.

Over the next centuries the Chinese developed fire lances, bombs with iron casings and, by the late 13th century, the first true guns. The Song used these against the Jin and the Mongols, and the Mongols spread the knowledge west.

The spread across Eurasia:

  • It reached the Islamic world and Europe in the 13th century.
  • By the 15th century cannons were breaking castle walls; the Ottomans used them on Constantinople in 1453.
  • Portuguese traders brought firearms to Japan in 1543, where they changed the wars of the Warring States.

It is counted among the Four Great Inventions of China, with paper, printing and the compass. Gunpowder weapons favoured states that could pay for cannons and trained gunners, and so helped build the large empires of the early modern age.
